definition: The general task of predicting future or missing values in temporal data — overlapping with forecasting, imputation, and anomaly anticipation.
details: The general task of predicting future or missing values in temporal data — overlapping with forecasting, imputation, and anomaly anticipation.

explainer.lead: Time series prediction is the general task of predicting future or missing values in temporal data. It matters because it overlaps with forecasting, imputation and anomaly anticipation.

tiers.eli5: It's the broad job of guessing parts of a timeline you can't see, whether that's what comes next or a gap in the middle.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply the same temporal modelling machinery to forecast ahead, fill gaps, or flag upcoming anomalies; a pitfall is that these goals overlap, so the task must be scoped clearly before choosing a method.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, prediction estimates future or missing values in temporal data; it overlaps with forecasting, imputation and anomaly anticipation. No further formal guarantees are specified here.

explainer.example: Predicting a missing reading in the middle of a sensor log is time series prediction just as forecasting the next reading is.
